data.raw_response:
=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (multiple leaves clearly arise from a single node in a circular arrangement, visible in all images)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are grouped densely at the shoot tips rather than widely spaced along the stem)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (leaves are undivided single blades)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.): entire (margins are smooth, though some leaves show holes/damage)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (broadest point is near the middle, tapering toward both ends)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acuminate (tapering to a distinct, elongated point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (wedge-shaped, narrowing gradually toward the petiole)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (single midrib with lateral veins branching off)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): clearly visible, parallel, and regularly spaced curving toward the apex
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (surface reflects light distinctly)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (surface appears smooth without visible hairs)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles are distinct but do not extend significantly beyond the leaf blade)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (cylindrical cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (stem appears rigid and lignified)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (stem appears smooth)
    19. Stem color: brown (visible where not obscured by leaves or tags)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (no obvious ridges or rough texture)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules visible at the nodes)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no distinct swollen joint at the leaf base)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent
F. Notes: Some leaves exhibit irregular holes and missing sections along the margins.
